newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico shares rise to record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico shares rise to record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks surged to a record close for a second day Tuesday, buoyed by gains in big name companies and forecasts for a fall in primary interest rates.
Analysts urged caution, however, saying that gains could be a short-lived New Year phenomenon.
"It was basically Telmex and Carso, again, although forecast rate falls at the primary auction obviously helped," a trader said.
The blue chip index closed up 23.96 points, or 0.69 percent, at 3,516.13. Volume was moderate at 82.1 million shares traded.

Telecommunications firm Telmex and holding company Grupo Carso closed up 32 centavos (4 cents) and 40 centavos (5 cents), respectively, at 14.32 pesos ($1.83) and 45.80 pesos ($5.48). Telmex ADRs gained 3/8 to 36-1/4 on Wall Street.

A Reuters survey of money market traders showed an average forecast rate of 24.78 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes, Treasury bills, at Tuesday evening's primary auction, or 0.93 percentage points below last week's rate.

Analysts said while Mexican stocks had lagged behind their counterparts in New York and a rally was overdue, Monday's and Tuesday's gains could still be mainly due to fund managers rearranging portfolios in the New Year.
Traders and analyst noted that Mexican stocks pared gains at midsession as the Dow Jones slumped, but managed to stay ahead on foreign investors stepping into the market.
"Just look at the exchange rate, foreigners are obviously buying Mexican stocks," a Finamex analyst said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.3 centavos firmer, at 7.8380 per dollar.
On the broad market, a total of 110 stocks changed hands, and gainers outnumbered decliners by 46 to 43.

At the head of the gainers, analysts noted the presence of paper firm Kimber and cement makers Apasco, up 6.30 pesos (80 cents) and 1.60 pesos (20 cents), respectively, at 55.70 pesos ($7.11) and 161.80 pesos ($20.64).
"Foreigners like Kimber and especially Apasco, as it is owned by Holderbank," said Jesus Almazan, an analyst at the Bursametrica consultant firm.
Pharmaceutical stock Autrey was second on the decliners list, down 86 centavos ($10.97) at 15.64 pesos ($2.00), in what traders said was profit-taking. Autrey headed the leaders' list on Monday.
The Most heavily traded decliner was financial stock GFB B series, off 3 centavos (1 cent) at 3.13 pesos (40 cents).
